result:
Understood. I'll write it up right after this one choice: how it gets built changes what goes in the document.

**1. Add it to the existing taproom app (recommended).** New batch, sack and bottling tables go in the same SQLite database on the Pi, with a few new pages. A cheap USB or Bluetooth barcode scanner acts like a keyboard, so scanning a sack's lot number is just a field that fills itself. You'd have one app, one database and one backup routine. The downside is that the tabs and the brewing records share the Pi, so if it fails, both go down together. Recall records matter more than tabs, so the design would include an off-Pi backup either way.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** It would use the same tools with its own database, so a problem in one can't touch the other. You'd have two things to update and back up, and no real gain unless you expect to split them onto different machines later.

**3. Off-the-shelf brewery software.** It has more features out of the box, but it means a monthly fee, your data on someone else's service, and it ignores what you already run. Since you know exactly what you want, I'd drop this one.

I recommend 1 because it builds on what's already working and keeps traceability in one place you control.

This is project-sized, so I'll write the full design into `specs/` and have a reviewer read it before you see it. I may come back once with a few questions from that. One heads-up: this folder isn't under git yet, so I'll offer to set that up so the spec can be committed.

Which way do you want to go?
